stem:
Rudra multiplies $\dfrac{6}{35} \times \dfrac{14}{9}$ and wants to cancel common factors before multiplying.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: Multiply $6 \times 14$ and $35 \times 9$ first, and leave every common factor uncancelled.
Cancel a common factor $7$ between $14$ and $35$, leaving $\dfrac{6}{5} \times \dfrac{2}{9}$.
Cancel a common factor $3$ between $6$ and $9$, leaving $\dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{15}$.
Treat the product as a sum of the two fractions instead of a product.

teacher.key_rationale: Cancel 7 from 14 and 35, then 3 from 6 and 9, to reach 4/15. Skipping all cancellation, or switching to addition, miss simplify-before-multiply.
